testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When facing an aggressive driver, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact—this may anger them more. Ignore any hand gestures they make.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo?

options.text: On the front, rear, and both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and both sides.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on all four sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo—front, rear, and both sides. This makes them visible from any direction.

questions.question: What is the purpose of tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Tie-downs secure cargo so it does not shift or fall off while driving. Shifting cargo can affect how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Move forward straight, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then move forward to the left.
Move forward straight, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward straight, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first move forward straight, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must end up fully within the parking space lines.

questions.question: When loading cargo, what is important to know?

options.text: Stack items as high as possible.
The weight limit your vehicle's suspension system can handle.
Place light items under heavy items.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight limit your vehicle's suspension system can handle.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. Know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry, including its suspension system limit.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve, slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver involved in a crash ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance away, wait for police to arrive, and report the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: When is drowsy driving most common?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving happens most often at night because people are naturally less alert during their normal sleep hours. Take precautions if you must drive at night.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Move forward straight, then back up straight.
Back up straight, then move forward to the left.
Move forward straight, then back up to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward straight, then back up to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, first move forward straight, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must end up fully within the parking space lines.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early, well before turning or changing lanes.
Keep signaling until the turn or lane change is complete.
Don't signal if no one is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't signal if no one is nearby.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals, even if no one appears to be nearby. Signal early, keep signaling through the entire turn or lane change, and turn off the signal when you finish.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts shows that they may be loose.

questions.question: What is allowed while driving?

options.text: You cannot write texts, but you can read them.
You can write texts, but you cannot read them.
You cannot write or read texts.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot write or read texts.
questions.explanation: You cannot text while driving. Texting means typing text into or reading text from an electronic device.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The trailer disconnects from the truck.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, tires can lose grip and slide on water. This is hydroplaning. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?
questions.explanation: Do not react to angry gestures from other drivers. Avoid eye contact and do not race them.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, pull the yellow, diamond-shaped knob to apply the parking brake. Push it in to release the brake.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Drive with a second person who can help with driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with a second person who can help with driving.
questions.explanation: Having a second driver reduces fatigue for both drivers. Avoid heavy foods and keep the cab cool to stay alert.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. It helps you see if your brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: Which is not a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: Tire failure signs include a loud bang, heavy thumping, or vibration. Heavy steering or the rear sliding means you should stop and check your tires.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, leakage should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, the vehicle needs repair before you drive it.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the tire itself

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late, what should you do?
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress by taking a deep breath. Accept that you will be late and continue driving safely.

questions.question: When alley docking, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: First, pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the parking space.

questions.question: If turning to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Not brake, because it may lock the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not brake, because it may lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning quickly to avoid a hazard. Braking can lock the wheels and cause your vehicle to skid out of control.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, when does air pressure enter the brake chambers?

options.text: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
When the driver uses the emergency brake.
When the driver uses the trailer hand valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than ____ psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, air should not leak faster than 5 psi in one minute. If it does, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you while driving a large vehicle, do all of the following except:
questions.explanation: If tailgated, slow down and increase your following distance. Do not speed up—this will only make the other driver tailgate at higher speeds.

questions.question: When pulled over on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Rely on your taillights to warn other drivers.
Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. Place warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: If you see a law enforcement vehicle on the side of the road with flashing lights, you should:
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on the side of the road, move away from that lane if possible. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless transporting hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless traveling through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
One air brake system with two different sets of controls.
One air brake system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the rear axle brakes. The other controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring during inspection?

options.text: The driver can drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is repaired.
The vehicle is safe to drive because most of the spring is still there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is repaired.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check the leaf springs for broken or missing leaves. This is a serious safety problem. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from any leaf spring, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes. Other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998 must also have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: How should you perform a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: You don't always need to check all items.

questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the proper steps and makes sure you don't forget to check anything important.

questions.question: How should you apply the brake pedal when coming to a stop?
questions.explanation: When stopping, push the brake pedal down gradually. Gradual braking helps you keep proper control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What can happen if you have more than one driver's license?

options.text: You probably won't get caught because many people have licenses.
You are not doing anything wrong.
You may be fined or jailed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be fined or jailed.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information through a computer system to prevent multiple licenses for one person. If you have more than one license, a court may fine you up to $5,000 or put you in jail.

questions.question: When should you shift into a lower gear when traveling down a steep hill?

options.text: Before you start the downhill grade.
After you have already started the grade.
As far down the grade as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the downhill grade.
questions.explanation: Shift into a low gear before you start going downhill. Be ready for gravity to speed up your vehicle when traveling downhill.

questions.question: When are you most likely to encounter strong winds?
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. Strong wind is especially a problem when coming out of a tunnel.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces is the most slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when it is warm enough to slightly melt ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low pressure warning device. A wig wag is one type of warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view if air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before you drive, check each slack adjuster after parking and setting the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to make sure it moves no more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, a driver should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if the vehicle is parked on a slope.

questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: If driving on a surface with poor traction, a driver should accelerate slowly:

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
So that they do not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly in poor traction conditions like rain or snow. This helps prevent losing control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required for vehicles that are transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Emergency equipment is required on all vehicles. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is properly charged and rated.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends mainly on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: When putting out an electrical fire, you should:
questions.explanation: Use a B:C fire extinguisher on electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: On a vehicle with a trailer, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailer is straight. Check mirror adjustment before every trip.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
Protect drivers' heads when they are entering the cab of a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board protects the driver from cargo moving forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: When asked to make a lane change during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Make the change as soon as the examiner asks, without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
Make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if that means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, check traffic, use your turn signal, and change lanes only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to make a lane change:

options.text: You should not be concerned with other motorists.
You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
You should make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if that means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: Check traffic, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes only when it is safe to do so.
